heading: Mortgage protection vs. PMI in 72 seconds
name: Mortgage protection vs. PMI: who each one protects
description: PMI protects the lender if you stop making payments. Mortgage protection is life insurance you own that pays the person you name. This short video compares them and lists three numbers to check before you buy.
transcript: Mortgage protection and PMI sound alike. Here is who each one protects. PMI protects the lender if you stop making payments. A lender may require it with less than 20 percent down. FHA and VA loans have their own versions. FHA loans require mortgage insurance. On VA loans, VA backing takes its place. Like PMI, they protect the lender, not you. Mortgage protection is different. It is life insurance that you own. It pays the person you name if you die during the term. PMI protects the lender. A lender may require it. Mortgage protection protects your family. It is optional. Watch the name. Ask who gets paid. Credit life sold with a loan pays the lender. A term policy you own pays your family. Before you buy, check three numbers. What you owe on the home. The years left on the loan. And the life insurance you already have. If there is a gap, a term policy sized to the loan is one way to fill it. Want to talk it through?
